title: Document Chunking Strategies & Boundary Optimization
description: Master fixed-size, recursive character, semantic, and syntax-aware chunking strategies with token overlap in .NET.

data.text: The Critical Role of Chunking in RAG

Chunking is the process of breaking a continuous document into discrete passages before embedding generation and indexing. It is often the single most impactful lever on RAG retrieval accuracy. If chunks are too small (e.g. 50 tokens), they lose surrounding context and generate ambiguous embeddings. If chunks are too large (e.g. 1500 tokens), they bundle multiple distinct topics together, diluting the embedding's semantic specificity and causing vector search to miss specific details.

data.title: The Chunk Overlap Rule
data.text: Always apply a 10% to 20% sliding window overlap between consecutive chunks. If a key sentence or relationship spans the boundary between Chunk A and Chunk B, the overlap ensures the semantic meaning is preserved in at least one of the vector representations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Chunking directly dictates the precision and recall of your vector search layer
Aim for 300 to 500 tokens per chunk for dense semantic retrieval in enterprise systems
Always apply 10% to 20% sliding window overlap to prevent context shearing across boundaries
Use recursive character splitting to respect natural semantic boundaries (paragraphs, sentences)
Prepend parent section headers (breadcrumbs) to chunks so individual fragments retain their structural context
data.takeaway: Optimal chunking balances granularity against comprehension. By leveraging recursive boundary detection and sliding window overlap, .NET ingestion pipelines preserve semantic coherence.
